newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index soars to record 4,724.59 pts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index soars to record 4,724.59 pts.

text.p: A strong bullish trend on the Budapest Stock Exchange continued on Thursday as foreigners remained active and recent strong gains also attracted domestic institutional and small investors' interest, traders said.
The BUX index soared to the 14th daily record high in a row, closing at 4,724.59, up 161.76 points or 3.55 percent.
"There is a euphoria on the bourse," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker.

Traders said that the bull-run was driven by a rising trend on the world's bourses, good macroeconomic figures, underpinned by November current account data released on Wednesday, and improving corporate performances.

Schuszter said that these factors firmed foreign investors' confidence in the market, and U.S. investment funds also increased their activity as Moody's granted investment grade to Hungary late last year.
Traders added that the bourse must seem a more attractive opportunity for taking profits for Hungarian small investors than ever.
"Even taxi-drivers say it is worth buying shares," said Peter Haas of Postabank Securities.
"We have an incredible number of orders," Schuszter said. "These are typical average people. I have never seen a swarming like that."

However, traders added that prices began to turn downwards at the end of the session, and larger number of the shares closed lower than it was usual recently, which may have been signs of a coming correction.
But the Hungarian bourse remained optimistic for the longer-term as traders believed corporate results to be published from the end of the month would be positive.
"1997 will be the year of rising certainly," Schuszter said.
